Walking Simulators - Are they still games?

If its interactive even to a very slim degree then yes its a game, not many people would argue that Zork isn't a game all be it a very different game than what you'd find today but its still a game none the less. My personal opinion is that the walking sim genre simply isn't fun because the developers often spend way more time trying to create narrative that pleases members of the gaming press rather than gameplay that would interest me but games are the new medium with the lowest barrier to entry so we are going to see an awful lot of pretentious crap over the next several years.

If you think about it writing a book, making a movie, making a TV show, making a stageplay, making music requires talent, skill, passion, money, substantial effort, enormous dedication, and luck before you even start making a living off it all while having to know the right people to get your career going. Games development just requires that you can follow tutorials and write a little code, you don't even need to be all that great at creating your own assets there are market places built around Unity and UDK where you can get almost anything you want and put you in contact with people capable of creating what you want and with a mainstream gaming press whose only function is to be a marketing tool and will sell you their voice for a very cheap price.

Should they exist? Fuck yes, I like my hobby so much that I'd like more people to be a part of it and understand its appeal even if they don't like the same things that I like about it. There is room in this world for walking simulators (probably not as much room as some people think) but just don't annoy me when I don't give a shit to play them.
